steps.text: Stir chocolate, instant coffee, and salt together in a medium bowl.
Heat cream, sugar, and vanilla in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it just begins to simmer.
Pour hot cream mixture over chocolate mixture; let sit for 1 minute.
Whisk chocolate and cream mixture for 1 to 2 minutes, until combined.
Pour mixture into four small espresso cups. Tap to remove any air bubbles. Chill thoroughly in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Serve topped with grated chocolate, or add lightly whipped cream and dust with cocoa powder.

review.reviewBody:
I love how quick an easy this is while being very elegant. Adding a little cayenne or mint or lemon/orange oil make for a different twist and flavour. Use the best chocolate you like for the best results.

For those that cannot get it to set or that the texture is grainy. The solution is get richer cream and different chocolate. The cream is the one that prevents the setting. heavy cream is in the 30% fat range. That is the requirement. You can try whipping cream BUT some have added sugars. The organic types usually do not. So do not skimp, use the good cream. As for the graininess this is usually the chocolate. It could be too old or simply of a lower quality. Again this is a high end desert, not chocolate pudding. Pay a few dollars a bar for 70%+ cocoa content. If you find it too bitter add more sugar the intensity of the chocolate is what you are looking for. Hope I helped.

This was so easy and delicious!!!! Chef John, you’ve done it again! I followed the directions exactly and watched the video—I think that helped a lot. Following the advice of other users I also used very good chocolate —Lindt 70% and dark. I tried whipping cream and heavy cream and found that I preferred the whipping cream as long as it was at least 30% cream. It was better with an accompaniment of lightly whipped cream and fresh raspberries. I also personally enjoyed it when it was only lightly set 2-3 hours vs. 4+ it continues to harden the longer you let it set and I liked it JUST set like thick pudding.

I didn’t have instant coffee so I substituted a little coffee liquor the first time I made this. It was amazing! Have made this too many times to count now. I did try it eventually with the instant coffee crystals but we prefer it without. Now I use a little Kahlua and some Baileys and steep a vanilla bean in the cream. Now that’s heaven!!! Looking for a good white chocolate recipe to try next.

I made this without the instant coffee and substituted 2T Rum which was heated then flamed to take some of the alcohol bite out of it. I also used semi-sweet chocolate because where I live is very rural and cannot buy bittersweet. I had semi-sweet on hand, broke it into pieces in the blender, added the heated cream and rum, then blended it up until smooth. It was wonderful.

Absolutely decadent! Truffles on a spoon! I topped mine with some grated white chocolate. Follow the instructions to a T and you won't have grainy chocolate or have it fail to set up. Don't over heat the cream, just to under a boil, stir constantly to dissolve the sugar, pour it over the chocolate, let sit for the full minute and whisk, whisk, whisk, until it starts to get a little thick. I put mine on the upper shelf in my fridge (the coldest part) and it was perfectly set in the four hours stated. Do use good quality chocolate, I used Lindt 70%. I also used Splenda instead of sugar. Wonderful results. Making this again, for sure! UPDATE! Made this substituting raspberry extract in place of the vanilla. AWESOME!!!!!

Very good. I had to use 2% Lactose free milk with 2 TBS corn starch since I’m lactose intolerant and it still turned out. Used orange zest instead of the coffee since husband doesn’t like the taste of coffee. Very decadent and perfect V Day dessert

OMG--this is far too easy to make, and therefore to eat ALL the time. Definitely choose good chocolate, because much of the taste will be affected by that choice. I followed the directions exactly, but actually divided it between five small ramekins and could have gone even smaller--it's so rich that a few bites are all that are needed if you're finishing off dinner. This is a very dense, intensely flavorful dessert that is smooth and creamy. NOT a light dish, but definitely delicious. My DH and DD both love it.

This is now my go-to company dessert! Soooo easy. Takes under 10 minutes to make. I use the Lindt 70% 3.5 oz bar, and skip the coffee. Use heavy cream, then add 3 teaspoons of Grand Marnier when I am about done whisking. Garnish with a generous blob of whipped cream, some orange zest on top. Raves from everyone!
Sarah's Bday '16, then 4.16.16 G&G. Ghiradelli 86% 1 + 1/3 of another. Used ramekins, could make 2 oz ramekins for 6 servings. Served with Cool Whip and a Lorna Doone. Rich rich rich

Okay, I made this loaded, rich, decadent dessert and at first thought, WOW, who do I know that can finish even a single serving? No one! So I experimented and after it had set up for a few hours in the fridge I drizzled, just a touch mind you, some Cointreau over the top, just enough to cover the top with the thinnest of layers. I left the serving in the fridge overnight and WOW! had turned into Holy Cow! just how delicious can anything taste. I LOVE THIS RECIPE!!!! And then, on my next try, I dropped about 1/2 teaspoon of PEANUT BUTTER in the bottom of the cup, filled it with the chocolate, and SURPRISED everyone at the table. I tell ya I'm a HERO around here. This recipe is endless!!!!

This was so easy to make--especially if you use bittersweet chocolate chips instead of buying a bar and chopping it. I had a 10 oz. bag of bittersweet chips and decided to use the entire bag so I increased all the other ingredients 2.5 times. I spooned the dessert into six ramekins. It set up very well. It could be made elegant looking by adding a dollop of whipped cream and some fresh raspberries or ribbons of orange peel. Tasted very good.

I do not know how people have issues with this recipe. Just FOLLOW the instructions and it turns out perfect everytime. I agree with others on using good chocolate. Such an easy dessert and looks like you spent a lot of time. *Restaurant tip… Add some flaky sea salt on top!
I made this recipe from the original in the Dec/Jan 2023 issue of AllRecipes. It was spectacular!

This was basically a bitter tasting chocolate truffle in cup form. I take full responsibility for the bitter taste. I used Ghiradelli 86% cocoa chocolate and Starbucks Via Italian Roast instant coffee. One problem is you can not taste and then adjust the bitterness because the sugar must dissolve in milk before pouring over the chocolate. If you added sugar later it would be grainy. But my main complaint is the the thickness. It was a struggle to get the spoon through the chocolate, although it did melt beautifully once in your mouth. This would be better served scooped and rolled like a truffle. Then you could add more sugar in the coating to offset the bitterness. I would not go any stronger than 70% cocoa next time.
I made it today, haven't tried it yet. Super easy to make. Hoping to wow my Valentine's.
Definitely decadent, elegant and the perfect end to a meal.
turned out horribly. did not set up.

I have made this twice within the last week. The first time with instant coffee, however tonight I didn't have any coffee, oh well. This is one of the simplest, most elegant desserts I have ever made. Chef John is a genius!
